overall_assessment: None of the 28 sampled plans has personal data or an approval stamp left. The name_label, name_like and admin_date flags are false alarms: the journal title 'The Reading teacher', reference authors, an article title ending in 'Teacher Education', 'Godkjent av Dekan' with no name after it, and the date in a festschrift title. A scan of all 1238 USN offerings found no staff name, e-mail address or phone number left, and the 2-digit approval stamps and name/role blocks (#305, #309) are now removed; the phone flags are spaced ISBNs and YYYYMMDD dates. The defects in the sample are cosmetic: Leganto type labels still stuck to titles that start with a quote mark or a lowercase letter, a stray ' .' where a date was removed, and cohort years ('kull 2017'). Some problems occur only outside the sample, so they cannot be reported as findings: (1) the academic-year rule still deletes Leganto year-month dates whose month equals the year + 1 ('2001-02-01' becomes '-01'; 77 removals in 50 offerings) and one page range ('3557-3558'); (2) the dd.mm.yyyy rule deletes the publication dates of newspaper and web references (about 100 dates in 36 offerings; 'Razsviet, 4.11.1923' becomes 'Razsviet, .'); (3) approval stamps with a month name but no day ('Godkjent desember 2017.'; 11 offerings) and 'November 2020:' stamps in the change log (19 offerings) stay in.

findings.evidence: ArticleiPed: Pedagogy for Digital Text Production … Article“Her story was complex”: A Twine workshop for ten- to twelve-year-old girls
findings.description: Leganto's item-type label is boilerplate that .anon_usn() should strip (#287, #306). It stays stuck to the title when the title starts with a curly or straight single quote, a curly double quote, a lowercase letter or a URL. Examples in the packet: 'Article“Translanguaging” and the implications for the future teaching of English in Norway' (courses 9–11 and 14–16), 'ArticleiPed: …' and 'Article“Her story was complex”: …' (courses 12 and 17). This happens in 8 of the 28 sampled courses and in all their English reading lists. Across all USN offerings, about 410 lines in 218 of 1238 offerings (18%) are affected. 237 lines in 135 offerings have a quote or URL after the label ('Book Chapter'Race', racism and representation', 'Website‘Curriculum in English (ENG01-04)’', 'Websitehttps://…'). About 175 lines in 105 offerings have lowercase after the label ('Book Chapterhistoriekultur', 'Websitenaturfag', 'E-bookut', 'Electronic Articlespelereglar'). This is not personal data, but the first word of each such title is wrong ('ArticleiPed', 'Book Chapterintercultural'), which affects tokens, word counts and title matching.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: R/anonymize.R .anon_usn(): the label rule requires the next character to match the lookahead '(?=[\p{Lu}\d"«(])'. A title that starts with ‘ ’ ' “ ”, a lowercase letter or 'http' does not match, so the label stays. The list of labels itself is complete: no unlisted Leganto type was found in USN text.
findings.suggested_fix: In .anon_usn(), widen the lookahead to '(?=[\p{Lu}\d"«(‘’'“”]|https?:)'. Add a second rule for lowercase-led titles, restricted to labels that never start an ordinary word: str_remove_all("(?m)^(?:Book Chapter|Book Extract|Electronic Book|Electronic Article|Newspaper Article|Government Document|E-book|Website|Article(?!s\\b))(?=\\p{Ll})", ...). Do not extend it to Map/Video/Note/Book/Document, which would hit 'Mappeinnlevering', 'Videoen', 'Notes', 'Books' and 'Documents'. Add tests to test-anonymize.R for 'Article“Translanguaging” and …', 'ArticleiPed: Pedagogy …', 'Book Chapter'Race', racism …' and 'Websitehttps://www.edutopia.org/…'. Add negative cases for 'Articles', 'Mappeinnlevering' and 'Videoen'.

findings.evidence: oppfølging på campus. Emneplan godkjent [−15.03.2024.−] . Litteratur
findings.description: Removing a date or a semester label that ends a sentence leaves a space before the full stop. 'Emneplan godkjent 15.03.2024.' becomes 'Emneplan godkjent .' (course 5). In the truncated part of course 3, 'ble brukt til MG1NO1 høsten 2020.' becomes 'ble brukt til MG1NO1 .'. The removal itself is correct, since these are admin dates. Across USN there are 58 new ' .' in 41 offerings. Most are harmless ('Godkjent av dekan .', 'Emnet går for første gang . Endringer er godkjent av dekan .'). A few now read wrongly, because the semester was what the sentence said: 'Faget går .', 'Resten blir pensum på PEL3, .', 'Også brukt .', 'Til utforskende praksisperiode .'. The dd.mm.yy rules already handle this with .eol_stop, so in course 6 '20.03.23.' leaves a clean 'Emneplan godkjent'.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: R/anonymize.R .anon_generic(): the dd.mm.yyyy rule '(?<![\d./])\d{1,2}\.\d{1,2}\.\d{4}…' and the season+year rule '\b(?i:<season>)\s*\d{4}\b' remove only the date. They leave the space before it, and (unlike the dd.mm.yy rules) they have no .eol_stop.
findings.suggested_fix: In .anon_generic(), let both rules also take the horizontal space before the match: prefix the patterns with '[ \t]*'. The space after the match is kept, so words do not glue. Also append .eol_stop to the dd.mm.yyyy rule, as the dd.mm.yy rules do. Then 'Emneplan godkjent 15.03.2024.' becomes 'Emneplan godkjent' and 'Faget går høsten 2021.' becomes 'Faget går.'. Add both to test-anonymize.R and check tar_read(metrics_check) for the change.

findings.description: A cohort year is administrative dating, like an academic year or a semester label, but it stays in when it is written as 'kull YYYY' in running text. The same plans already lose the year in '(Kull 2018 HØST)', because there it is followed by a season word. The packet has one example (course 4, Vår 2020: 'informasjonsskriv til studenter kull 2017'). Across USN, 30 offerings keep a cohort year ('Pedagogikk og elevkunnskap 5-10, kull 2022, 1. år (MG2PE1) Porsgrunn', 'Ingen godkjenning foreligger for kull 2018'). Outside the sample, the same keyword-plus-year rule also misses approval stamps that have a month name but no day, in 11 offerings: 'Godkjent desember 2017.', 'Emneplan godkjent mars 2022.', 'Godkjent nov 21.', 'Godkjent og akkreditert aug 21'. The month-year change-log stamps in 'Endringsbeskrivelse' ('November 2020: Endring i forkunnskapskrav …', 19 offerings) also stay.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: R/anonymize.R .anon_generic(): the admin-year rule '((?i:opprettet|oppdatert|revidert|vedtatt|godkjent|gjeldende(?: fra)?|gyldig(?: fra)?|sist …))\s+\d{4}\b' needs one of its keywords directly before a 4-digit year. 'kull' is not one of the keywords, and a month name between 'godkjent' and the year breaks the match. .long_dates_regex needs a day ('7. juni 2016'). No rule targets a 'Month YYYY:' prefix at the start of a line.
findings.suggested_fix: In .anon_generic(), change the admin-year rule to: str_replace_all(paste0("((?i:opprettet|oppdatert|revidert|vedtatt|godkjent(?: og akkreditert)?|kull(?:et)?|gjeldende(?: fra)?|gyldig(?: fra)?|sist (?:endret|revidert|oppdatert)))(?:[ \\t]+", .month_abbrev_regex, "\\.?[ \\t]+(?:\\d{4}|\\d{2})|\\s+\\d{4})\\b", .not_gov, .eol_stop), "\\1"). Here .month_abbrev_regex is .month_regex plus jan|feb|mar|apr|jun|jul|aug|sep|okt|nov|des. The 2-digit year is accepted only after a month, so 'kull 20 studenter' stays. In .anon_usn(), drop a change-log date prefix: str_remove_all("(?im)^[ \\t]*(?:januar|februar|mars|april|mai|juni|juli|august|september|oktober|november|desember)[ \\t]+\\d{4}[ \\t]*[:–-][ \\t]*"). Add tests for 'informasjonsskriv til studenter kull 2017', 'Godkjent desember 2017.', 'Godkjent nov 21.' and 'November 2020: Endring i forkunnskapskrav'. Record the cohort-year choice in methods.qmd.
